messages:
incident-bot: Paging: High p99 latency observed for /v1/stream from us-west-2 shared-gpu pool (alert: streaming.p99 > 2s for 5m). Graph: https://grafana.company/streaming/p99?org=1 :rotating_light:
Alex: ack — oncall for us-west-2, joining.
Maya: I'm on it. does the alert show increased error rate or just latency?
Jordan: mainly latency spike, error rate slight uptick (5xx ~0.4% -> 1.2%). p95 ~ 260ms -> 450ms, p99 ~ 1.8s -> 7.2s at the peak.
Kim: looking at runtime logs now, seeing streaming stalls with repeated `KVCache miss` spikes and GPU copy stalls.
Alex: any customer-facing incidents yet? Lee?
Lee: 3 tickets opened within last 10m saying streams froze then resumed, one customer says session aborted and they got 502s. I'll start templated outreach once we confirm scope.
Maya: can someone run host-level IO and GPU checks on nodes in the shared pool? suspect noisy neighbor cgroup/io saturation.
Jordan: running quick checks on node gpu-shared-12: attaching outputs:
```
# iostat -x 1 3
Device:         rrqm/s wrqm/s   r/s   w/s  rMB/s  wMB/s avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await r_await w_await svctm  %util
nvme0n1         0.00   72.00  1.00  85.00  0.01   1.20    28.8     6.2  72.1  10.2  3.4   1.20  98.7
```
and `nvidia-smi dmon -s u` shows GPU memory copies pegged and `cudaMemcpy` stalls in runtime.
Kim: also seeing cgroup.io throttling metrics high for container `tenant-big-batch-7` (throttle_time > 5000ms). likely heavy writeback/flush bursts.
Alex: can we identify top IO offenders on that host? `pmap`/`iotop`?
Jordan: `iotop -boP` shows PID 45233 (tenant-big-batch-7) writing ~800MB/s bursts, average ~250MB/s sustained for short periods.
Maya: that's our noisy neighbor. Impact path: tenant saturates NVMe bandwidth -> kernel flush delays -> GPU DMA stalls -> streaming stalls -> increased tail lat.
Alex: live mitigations? suggestions: throttle IO via cgroup, evict/evacuate pod to dedicated pool, or fallback requests to dedicated capacity region.
Kim: quick mitigation I can apply: set io.weight lower for that container and set `blkio.throttle.read_bps_device`/`write_bps` limits. can push a QoS cgroup with limit 50MB/s to reduce bursts.
Hunter: product note — if we throttle too hard streaming clients may see buffering, prefer routing to dedicated with slightly higher latency but stable.
Maya: do we have capacity in dedicated pool in us-west-2?
Jordan: small spare headroom in dedicated-gpu-2; we can move a few streams over. migration will drop current ephemeral connections though.
Alex: sequence: 1) apply soft IO throttle to noisy container, 2) start moving highest-priority customers to dedicated pool, 3) enable streaming fallback route for others.
Kim: applying soft throttle now to PID 45233 (container id 9f3c):
```
echo "8:0 52428800" > /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/container-9f3c/blkio.throttle.write_bps_device
# set io.weight lower
echo 100 > /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/container-9f3c/blkio.weight
```
Applying...
Alex: keep us posted.
(30s later)
Kim: throttle applied. iostat shows device avgqu-sz dropping from 6.2 -> 1.1 and io util down to ~32%.
Jordan: p99 dropped from 7.2s -> 2.1s within 90s of throttle. p95 back to ~320ms.
Maya: good. start evacuating tenant pods off shared pool to dedicated-gpu-2 for long term.
Jordan: triggering k8s evict on the pod + taint nodes and schedule to dedicated pool: `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data pod/tenant-big-batch-7` then recreate with nodeSelector `dedicated=true`.
Kim: eviction started. note: there will be short reconnects for active streaming sessions for that tenant — Lee pls include in comms.
Lee: on it — messaging customers now, telling them brief interruption while we migrate to stable pool.
(10m later)
Jordan: eviction completed, pod recreated on dedicated-gpu-2. verify: `kubectl get pods -o wide` shows new node.
Alex: what's the state of the shared pool? any residual tail?
Maya: monitoring shows p99 now ~450ms and stable, no new 5xx spikes. streaming latency graph back to baseline.
incident-bot: Incident update: mitigation applied (IO throttle + tenant migration); alert suppressed.
Hunter: product follow-up: we should add an automated QoS policy to detect sustained blkio bursts and auto-throttle or move tenant to dedicated plan. filing a feature ticket.
Maya: agree — also add a runbook step to check `blkio.throttle` and `nvidia-smi dmon` in first 5m for streaming p99 alerts.
Alex: temporary postmortem notes: root cause = tenant workload burst flushing NVMe causing kernel IO saturation -> GPU DMA stalls. Immediate fix = cgroup IO throttle + eviction to dedicated pool. Impact = a handful of customers experienced streaming stalls / transient 502s, one session aborted.
Lee: customer messages sent with status and ETA. will follow up with names + ticket references.
Kim: scheduling a follow-up to check disk wear and ensure tenant's workload has updated batching config to reduce writeback bursts.
Maya: transitioning to postmortem channel later — thanks all for quick reaction. :thumbsup:
Alex: resolving incident, leaving notes for handoff.
incident-bot: Incident resolved and marked recovered at 1745013600. Postmortem: /docs/incidents/1745009999-postmortem-draft.md
